paper.title: Active Hypothesis Testing for Correlated Combinatorial Anomaly Detection

settings.name_in_paper: Correlated combinatorial anomaly identification with designed linear measurements (fixed confidence)
unmapped: Goal: identify an unknown anomalous subset S* of size n (m in the vocabulary) among K streams; the hypothesis space is all n-subsets
Observation y_t = c_t^T x_t + noise, where x_t ~ N(mu_S*, Sigma) with a full known covariance Sigma (correlated noise); the observation variance c^T Sigma c depends on the action
The learner knows the covariance matrix Sigma, the nominal mean mu_0 and the anomaly signal pattern delta (the size of the mean shift)
The action set is the L1 ball {c : ||c||_1 <= B}; the learner knows the L1 action budget B (not a knapsack budget)
settings.definition_quote: At time $t$, the learner chooses a vector $\mathbf{c}_t \in \mathbb{R}^K$ and observes a scalar projection $y_t = \mathbf{c}_t^\top \mathbf{x}_t + \xi_t$, where $\mathbf{x}_t$ is the latent system state and $\xi_t$ is Gaussian noise with variance $\mathbf{c}_t^\top \bm{\Sigma} \mathbf{c}_t$. To model sensing or energy constraints, we restrict the action space to $\mathcal{C} = \{ \mathbf{c} \in \mathbb{R}^K : \|\mathbf{c}\|_1 \le B \}$.

symbols.Gamma_star: optimal information rate max_{c in C} min_{S' != S*} D(H_S* || H_S' | c), i.e. the Chernoff information of the best measurement

conditions: the proof also relies on Assumptions E.1-E.3 (effective rank r_eff(Sigma)/K >= eps, incoherence, bounded signal ratio)
tuning: GLR stopping rule with threshold beta(t,delta) = log(1/delta) + O(log log(1/delta))

source.label: thm:nonasymptotic
source.quote: Assume that $\bm{\Sigma}$ is positive definite and the action set $\mathcal{C}$ is compact. For any $\delta \in (0,1)$, ECC-AHT is $\delta$-correct, and its expected stopping time satisfies \mathbb{E}[\tau] \le \frac{\log(1/\delta)}{\Gamma^\star} + C_1 \log\log(1/\delta) + C_2, where $C_1$ and $C_2$ are constants independent of $\delta$.

results.notes: The algorithm is also stated to be delta-correct. Gamma_star is defined inconsistently: KL-based, with a factor of 1/2, in the main text, and as an SNR ratio without the 1/2 in the appendix proof. The proof is heuristic in places.

symbols.Gamma_star: optimal information rate max_{c in C} min_{S' != S*} D(H_S* || H_S' | c)

conditions: the proof also relies on Assumptions E.1-E.3
tuning: GLR stopping rule with threshold beta(t,delta) = log(1/delta) + o(log(1/delta))
results.notes: The theorem is stated as an equality. It is recorded as a limsup upper bound with the expression c*log(1/delta) and c = 1/Gamma_star.

cited_results.cited_title: Optimal best arm identification with fixed confidence
cited_results.setting_description: Fixed-confidence identification of the anomalous subset under correlated Gaussian noise with designed measurements; any delta-correct algorithm (classical Chernoff / Garivier-Kaufmann argument, also citing chernoff1959sequential)
